papers.title: International Trade: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on international trade, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: A country has a comparative advantage in a good when it can produce it
questions.explanation:
Comparative advantage compares opportunity costs, not total output.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- in larger quantities with the same resources: That is absolute advantage.
- and export it in the largest quantity: Export volume is not the test.
- and sell it at the highest world price: Price is not the test.

options.label: A
options.content: in larger quantities with the same resources

options.label: B
options.content: and export it in the largest quantity

options.label: C
options.content: at a lower opportunity cost than another country

options.label: D
options.content: and sell it at the highest world price

questions.stem: With the same resources, country A can produce 20 tonnes of rice or 10 bales of cloth. What is the opportunity cost of 1 tonne of rice in A?
questions.explanation:
1 tonne of rice costs $\dfrac{10}{20} = 0.5$ bales of cloth.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 2 bales of cloth: That is the opportunity cost of 1 bale of cloth in tonnes of rice.
- 10 bales of cloth: That is the total cloth A could make.
- 30 bales of cloth: You added the two outputs.

questions.stem: A country's export price index is 120 and its import price index is 150 (base year = 100). What are its terms of trade?
questions.explanation:
Terms of trade $= \dfrac{120}{150} \times 100 = 80$: they have worsened by 20%.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 125: You divided import prices by export prices.
- 30: You subtracted the indices.
- 270: You added the indices.

questions.stem: A tariff is
questions.explanation:
Tariffs raise the price of imports and earn revenue for the government.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a limit on the quantity of a good that may be imported: That is a quota.
- a complete ban on imports: That is an embargo.
- a payment to local producers: That is a subsidy.

options.label: A
options.content: a limit on the quantity of a good that may be imported

questions.stem: The infant industry argument for protection says that
questions.explanation:
Once the industry grows large and efficient, protection should be removed.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- old industries should be protected for ever: The argument is for temporary protection of new industries.
- all exports should be banned: It is about imports competing with new industries.
- wages should be raised in new industries: It is about competition, not wages.

options.label: A
options.content: new industries need temporary protection until they can compete

options.label: B
options.content: old industries should be protected for ever

options.label: D
options.content: wages should be raised in new industries

questions.stem: International trade differs from internal trade because international trade
questions.explanation:
Currencies must be exchanged, and payments recorded in the balance of payments.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- never involves transport costs: International trade usually has higher transport costs.
- faces no tariffs or quotas: Tariffs and quotas apply to international trade.
- uses only one legal system: Each country has its own laws.

questions.stem: A bag of imported rice costs NLe 600 when it lands. What is its price after a 20% import tariff?
questions.explanation:
Price = 600 + 20% of 600 = 600 + 120 = NLe 720.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 620 NLe: You added NLe 20 instead of 20%.
- 120 NLe: That is the tariff only.
- 480 NLe: You subtracted the tariff.

questions.stem: Sierra Leone's main exports are
questions.explanation:
Minerals earn most of the country's export income; cocoa and coffee are important cash crops.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- petroleum products: Sierra Leone imports most of its fuel.
- rice: Sierra Leone imports much of its rice.
- machinery and vehicles: These are major imports.

options.label: D
options.content: minerals such as iron ore, rutile and diamonds

papers.topic: Balance of Payments and Exchange Rates
papers.title: Balance of Payments and Exchange Rates: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on balance of payments and exchange rates, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: A country exports goods worth US$900 million and imports goods worth US$1,300 million. What is its balance of trade?
questions.explanation:
Balance of trade = exports − imports of goods = 900 − 1,300 = −US$400 million (a deficit).

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 400 US$ million: Imports are larger than exports, so the balance is negative (a deficit).
- 2200 US$ million: You added exports and imports.
- 1300 US$ million: That is the value of imports.

questions.stem: The balance of trade records
questions.explanation:
The balance of trade is the visible part of the current account.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- all transactions with the rest of the world: That is the balance of payments.
- trade in services only: Services are invisible trade, part of the current account.
- flows of investment and loans: Those are in the capital and financial account.

options.label: A
options.content: exports and imports of goods only

options.label: B
options.content: all transactions with the rest of the world

questions.stem: Money sent home by Sierra Leoneans working abroad is recorded in the
questions.explanation:
Remittances are one-way transfers with nothing given in return.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- capital and financial account: That records investment and loans.
- official reserves: Reserves are held by the central bank.
- balance of trade: The balance of trade covers goods only.

options.label: B
options.content: current account (as secondary income or transfers)

questions.stem: The exchange rate is NLe 24 = US$1. How many leones does US$500 cost?
questions.explanation:
500 × 24 = NLe 12,000.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 20.83 NLe: You divided instead of multiplying.
- 524 NLe: You added the numbers.
- 476 NLe: You subtracted the numbers.

questions.stem: Devaluation is
questions.explanation:
Devaluation is a government or central bank decision; depreciation happens in the market.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a fall in a currency's value caused by market forces: That is depreciation.
- an official increase in the value of a currency: That is revaluation.
- a cut in the central bank's interest rate: That is a monetary policy action.

options.label: A
options.content: a fall in a currency's value caused by market forces

options.label: B
options.content: an official increase in the value of a currency

options.label: C
options.content: an official reduction in the value of a currency under a fixed exchange rate

options.label: D
options.content: a cut in the central bank's interest rate

questions.stem: A depreciation of the leone against the US dollar makes
questions.explanation:
More leones are needed per dollar, so imports cost more at home.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- imports cheaper in leones: Each dollar of imports now costs more leones.
- exports dearer to foreign buyers: Exports become cheaper in foreign currency.
- no difference to trade: Prices of traded goods change.

options.label: D
options.content: imports dearer in leones and exports cheaper to foreign buyers

questions.stem: A main function of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is to
questions.explanation:
The IMF also promotes exchange rate stability and advises on economic policy.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- give long-term loans for development projects: That is the World Bank's role.
- issue the leone: The Bank of Sierra Leone issues the leone.
- run the ECOWAS free trade scheme: That is an ECOWAS institution's role.

options.label: A
options.content: give short- and medium-term loans to countries with balance of payments problems

options.label: B
options.content: give long-term loans for development projects

options.label: D
options.content: run the ECOWAS free trade scheme

questions.stem: A country has a visible balance of −400, a services balance of −200, net primary income of −120 and net transfers of +420 (US$ million). What is its current account balance?
questions.explanation:
Current account = −400 − 200 − 120 + 420 = −US$300 million (a deficit).

**Why the other options are wrong**

- -720 US$ million: You left out the transfers.
- 300 US$ million: The current account is in deficit, so the balance is negative.
- 1140 US$ million: You added all the figures as if they were positive.

papers.title: Economic Growth, Development, and Planning: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on economic growth, development, and planning, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: Economic development differs from economic growth because development
questions.explanation:
Growth is quantitative (more output); development is qualitative as well (better lives).

**Why the other options are wrong**

- means only a rise in real GDP: That is economic growth.
- means only a rise in population: Population growth is not development.
- refers only to the short run: Development is a long-term process.

options.label: A
options.content: means only a rise in real GDP

options.label: B
options.content: includes improvements in welfare such as health, education and less poverty

options.label: C
options.content: means only a rise in population

options.label: D
options.content: refers only to the short run

questions.stem: The Human Development Index (HDI) combines measures of
questions.explanation:
The HDI measures a long and healthy life, knowledge and a decent standard of living.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- GDP, inflation and unemployment: These are not the HDI's three dimensions.
- population, exports and imports: These are not part of the HDI.
- birth rate, death rate and migration: These are population measures.

options.label: C
options.content: life expectancy, education and income per head

options.label: D
options.content: birth rate, death rate and migration

questions.stem: In the vicious circle of poverty, low income leads directly to
questions.explanation:
Low income → low saving → low investment → little capital → low productivity → low income.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- high investment: Low saving means low investment.
- high productivity: Productivity stays low.
- high saving: People with low incomes can save little.

questions.stem: A common characteristic of developing countries is
questions.explanation:
Most workers are in agriculture, and exports are mainly minerals and cash crops.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- high income per head: Income per head is low.
- slow population growth: Population usually grows fast.
- a large manufacturing sector: Manufacturing is usually small.

questions.stem: A rolling plan is a development plan that is
questions.explanation:
Rolling plans adapt to changing conditions.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- fixed for twenty years without change: That describes a rigid long-term plan.
- made up only of compulsory targets: That describes imperative planning.
- limited to a single sector: That is a partial (sectoral) plan.

options.label: A
options.content: fixed for twenty years without change

options.label: B
options.content: revised every year, with a new year added as each year ends

options.label: C
options.content: made up only of compulsory targets

questions.stem: Tied aid is aid that
questions.explanation:
Tied aid may be dearer or less suitable than goods bought elsewhere.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- is a grant with no conditions: That is untied aid.
- is a short-term loan from the IMF: IMF loans are not what tied aid means.
- can be spent only within ECOWAS: Tied aid is tied to the donor country.

options.label: A
options.content: is a grant with no conditions

options.label: B
options.content: is a short-term loan from the IMF

options.label: C
options.content: must be spent on goods and services from the donor country

options.label: D
options.content: can be spent only within ECOWAS

questions.stem: A country's real GDP rises from NLe 25,000 million to NLe 26,000 million in a year. What is its rate of economic growth?
questions.explanation:
Growth rate $= \dfrac{26000 - 25000}{25000} \times 100 = 4\%$.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 1000 %: That is the increase in NLe million, not the percentage.
- 3.85 %: You divided by the new GDP; divide by last year's.
- 104 %: That is the new GDP as a percentage of the old.

questions.stem: "Brain drain" refers to
questions.explanation:
The country loses doctors, engineers and teachers it trained at great cost.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- the movement of unskilled workers from villages to towns: That is rural–urban migration.
- the transfer of money out of the country: That is capital flight.
- a fall in school enrolment: That is not what brain drain means.

options.label: A
options.content: the movement of unskilled workers from villages to towns

options.label: B
options.content: the transfer of money out of the country

options.label: D
options.content: the emigration of skilled and educated people

papers.title: Economic Integration in West Africa: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on economic integration in west africa, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: A customs union differs from a free trade area because a customs union has
questions.explanation:
In a free trade area each member keeps its own tariffs on outsiders.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- free movement of labour and capital: That is added in a common market.
- a single currency: That belongs to an economic union.
- a single government: That is political union.

options.label: B
options.content: free movement of labour and capital

questions.stem: A common market adds to a customs union
questions.explanation:
Workers and capital can move freely to where they are most productive.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a common external tariff: A customs union already has this.
- the removal of tariffs between members: A free trade area already does this.
- a single government: That is political union.

options.label: B
options.content: free movement of labour and capital between members

options.label: C
options.content: the removal of tariffs between members

questions.stem: ECOWAS was established in
questions.explanation:
ECOWAS was founded on 28 May 1975.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 1963 by the OAU Charter: The OAU was founded in 1963, but ECOWAS was not.
- 1973 by the Mano River Declaration: That founded the Mano River Union.
- 2002 by the African Union: The AU was founded in 2002.

questions.stem: The headquarters of the ECOWAS Commission is in
questions.explanation:
The ECOWAS Commission is based in Abuja, Nigeria.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Freetown: Freetown is not the ECOWAS headquarters.
- Accra: Accra hosts the AfCFTA secretariat.
- Lagos: The treaty was signed in Lagos, but the headquarters is in Abuja.

questions.stem: The founding members of the Mano River Union in 1973 were
questions.explanation:
The union is named after the Mano River on the Liberia–Sierra Leone border.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Guinea and Sierra Leone: Guinea joined in 1980.
- Ghana and Nigeria: They are not MRU members.
- Côte d'Ivoire and Liberia: Côte d'Ivoire joined in 2008.

questions.stem: A major problem of economic integration in West Africa is that member countries
questions.explanation:
With similar exports, members have little to sell to each other.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- produce very different manufactured goods: Most produce similar primary goods, not varied manufactures.
- already share one currency: Most members have their own currencies.
- have excellent transport links: Poor transport links are a problem.

questions.stem: The ECOWAS protocol on free movement allows citizens of member states to
questions.explanation:
Visa-free travel helps traders and workers move across the region.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- vote in other member states' elections: Voting rights are not included.
- avoid paying any taxes: Taxes still apply.
- settle permanently anywhere without any permit: Longer stays still need permits.

options.label: A
options.content: vote in other member states' elections

options.label: C
options.content: travel and stay in other member states without a visa for up to 90 days

options.label: D
options.content: settle permanently anywhere without any permit

questions.stem: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) aims to
questions.explanation:
Trading under the AfCFTA began in 2021, with its secretariat in Accra.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- introduce a single currency for West Africa: That is the aim of the West African Monetary Zone.
- provide peacekeeping forces: Peacekeeping is not its purpose.
- lend money for development projects: That is the role of development banks.

options.label: A
options.content: introduce a single currency for West Africa

options.label: D
options.content: create a single continental market for goods and services
